3. The Rule has been resisted by the Respondent Nos. 1, 2 and 4 by filing a combined affidavit-in-opposition denying the allegations in the petition and stating, inter alia. that Lakshmipur Mahila Colloege has been functioning regularly in a tin-shed on the land acquired and it reveals from the statement furnished by the principal of the College against the objection in reply to petition filed by the petitioner before the Minister of Land Administration that 0.36 acres of land affecting the plot Nos. 3730 and 3731 was donated by Dr. Montazuddin Chowdhury, (at present Vice Chancellor of Islamic University, Dhaka) by a registered deed dated 21.4.1985 along with a big tin shed in favour of the College. One Nurul Huda also donated 0.24 acres of land in the aforesaid plots by a registered deed dated 25.7.1985 to the College and the College has been functioning therein since 13.2,1985. The petitioner filed pre-emption case being' Miscellaneous Case No.71 of 1981 in the Court of the learned Subordinate Judge, Lakshmipur for the land purchased by Dr. Montazuddin Chowdhury which was allowed and against the said judgment an appeal was preferred before the District Judge, Noakhali being Miscellaneous Appeal No. 58 of 1986, which is still pending and it is not correct that there is any residential building or shed on the acquired land in question in plot Nos. 3730 and 3731 except big tin shed wherein the College has been 'functioning. There is no graveyard within the land in question but there is graveyard on the southern middle end of plot No. 3731 attached to the side ditch of C & B Road beyond the acquired land in question. It further appears from the records prepared by the land acquisition staff on 24.5.1986 after filed verification that 0.05 acre of Bhiti land covered by College shed, 0.17 acres Bagan land, 0.16 acres Chala land in Plot No. 3730 and 0.18 acre of Chala land in Plot No. 3731 have been affected by the acquisition which was originally recorded in the names of Abdul Karim, Abdul Rahman, Muslim Mia, son of Elahi Baksh, Shamsul Haque Mia, son of Mafizuddin, Mohammad Anwar Baksh son of Noor Mohammad Mia, Abdur Rahim, son of Abdul Ali, Habibur Rahman, son of Abdur Rahim and Helima Khatoon, wife of Abdur Rahim under SA Khatian No. 800 (CS Khatian No. 971) for an area of 0.71 acres in CS Plot No. 3730 and in the names of Noor Mohammad, Osi Mia, Abdur Rahim, son of Abdul Ali, Halima Khatoon, wife of Abdur Rahmim and Habibur Rahman, son of Abdur Rahim for an area of 0.47 acres under SA Khatian No: 784 (CS Khatian No. 941) in plot No. 3731 including some other plots of Mouza Banchha Nagar. The petitioner however, did not submit any claim or objection on receipt of the notice under section 6 of the Ordinance as to ascertain the quantum of his land affected in the plots or reported any facts before the land acquisition staff at the time of joint verification in the field on 24.5.1986 at the initial stage of the proceeding. There is no graveyard within the land acquired. Mr. Monsurul Haque is the principal of Lakshmipur Mahila College which is managed by a governing body. That there was a pressing need for a Mahili College at Lakshmipur and, as such, the College was started in the Poura Shahid Smriti School in 1984 and subsequently shifted to the shed donated by said Dr. Mantazuddin Chowdhury after making necessary repair and reconstruction of the shed by the college authority and about 38. girl students have appeared at the final HSC Examination this year under regular permission from the Board. When litigation was started in respect of the land in question wherein the college has already been established the governing body of the college resolved to go for acquisition of the land to keep the College free from any encumbrance and accordingly, the Principal has submitted a proposal for acquisition in a prescribed manner as per decision of the governing body dated 24.2.1984 and the matter relating to the acquisition of the land was placed before the District Land Allocation Committee, Lakshimpur for discussion and allotment of the land for the establishment of the Lakshmipur Mohila College. And considering public purpose for development of women's education in the district acquisition proceeding has been started vide RC No. 9/5-85 and notice under section 3 of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982 (II of 1982) was duly published on 28.5.1986 at the convenient places including the land in question calling upon objection against the acquisition proposal but neither the petitioner nor anybody of the recorded tenants filed any objection against the acquisition proposal within 15 days or thereafter and the Government vide Order No. General 1/84/102(68) Requisition dated 31.1.1984 accorded approval on 24.6.1986 confirming the acquisition proposal as provided under section 5(1) of the Ordinance. Thereafter notices under section 6 of the Ordinance were served upon the recorded owners on 15.7.1986 and published at the convenient place calling upon to submit interest in the property in question on 23.7.1986. The petitioner received the notice on 15.7.1986 but instead of submission of claim the petitioner filed an objection before the Minister of Land Administration. However, the objection petition was rejected on 16.1O.l986. The college authority has deposited the entire assessed amount to be paid as compensation, Munsurul Haque, the Principal of the College, has got nothing to do in the acquisition proceeding which was however, started in accordance with the provisions of the Acquistion and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance II of 1982. The petitioner resides with his family elsewhere and not on the plots in question. The petitioner is not the recorded tenant in respect of the suit plot and the name of the petitioner did not appear in the Khatian and, as such, has no right, title, interest and possession in the land in question under acquisition. The petitioner has no locus standi to file this writ petition challenging the acquisition of 0.56 decimal of land. The acquisition proceeding has been finalised as long back on 23.4.1988 when the District Land Acquisition Authority took possession of the acquired land by metes and bound after proper demarcation of land and also handed over possession of the same to the College authority on 23.4.1988, On 25.5.1991 the foundation stone of the main building for Lakshmipur Mahila College was laid ceremoniously by the then Deputy Commissioner, Lakshmipur for which the petitioner has filed a contempt case in the High Court Division against the Respondents being Contempt Case No. 3 of 1991 and, as such, the petitioner has full knowledge of the establishment of Lakshmipur Mahila College over the said plots. The Government also sanctioned Taka 31,06,004/85 for construction of two storied science building for the College and the acquisition of the said 0.56 decimal of land in those plots is now a factum valet as the said Mahila college has been functioning in the acquired land which has been acquired for the public purpose. 

 4. The petitioner filed affidavit-in-reply denying allegations and reiterated the statements made in the petition and further stated that the petitioner purchased 1.68 acres of land out of plot Nos. 3730, 3731 and 3732 of khatian No. 941,946 and 971 being MRR Khatian No. 784, 787 and 800 in his own name and in the names of his eldest son and wife who acquired title, amongst others, by kabala dated 20.11.56 and 3l.11.58 executed by Abdul Karim, a recorded tenant in the GS Khatian, kabala dated 20.11.1955 executed by Abdul Karim and his brother Abdul Alim and the brother of the petitioner also purchased some portion of the suit plots from the CS recorded tenant by kabala dated 9.6.70 executed by Mokbul Ahmed and kabala dated 3.8.70 executed by Md. Ismail and kabala dated 18.7.51 executed by Abdul Karim and they are in possession. The petitioner also got 0.56 acres of land in the said plots by way of pre-emption proceeding against Dr. Montazuddin and his brother Shamsul Islam, the purchasers from the Co- operative Society in Miscellaneous Case No. 71 of 1981 of the court of Subordinate Judge, Lakshimpur. Mr. Munsurul Haque, the principal of the college along with large number of people armed with various weapons, forcibly took possession of the land of the petitioner for which the petitioner filed contempt petition No.3 of 1991 before this Court and the same is awaiting disposal. 

 5. Mr. SR Pal, the learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submitted that the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982 laid down the procedure providing for publication of preliminary notice of acquisition of property in respect of any property in any locality if needed or likely to be needed for the specific public purpose or in the public interest and shall cause a notice to be published at convenient places in the prescribed form and manner stating the property is proposed to be acquired. Furthermore, the property to be acquired must be specified one for identification with sufficient particulars to indicate definitely which part of the plot is required with adequate description of the property so as to enable the owners or persons interested in the said property to file objection to the acquisition of the property. Mr. Pal elucidated with reference to Annexure-E and El section 6 of the Ordinance provides iliat when the acquiring authority has made a decision for acquisition of property under section 5 or under proviso to section 4(3)(b) as the case may be, the Deputy Commissioner shall cause public notice to be given in the prescribed manner at a convenient place stating that the authority has decided to acquire the property and intend to take possession thereof and that claims to compensation for the compensation for all interest to such property may be made to him. He has also referred to Annexure-A to the petition which are Khatian Nos. 971 and 941 respectively showing plot No. 3730 measuring 0.71 acres and plot No. 3841 measuring 0.90, plot No. 3731 measuring 0.47, plot No. 3732 measuring 0.20 acre and plot No. 3736 measuring 0.03 respectively and submitted that the authority must indicate definitely which part of the land is required by them out of the plot with adequate description sought to be acquired by them so as to notify owner to exact extent of the property sought to be taken and referred to the decision in the case of Sufia Khatun Vs. 'Secretary, Revenue Department & others 20 DLR (SC) 18. Mr. Pal next submitted with reference to the pre-emption case and the proceeding under section 144 CrPC initiated by Munsurul Haque in respect of the acquired land that on failure to get the land has mala fide initiated the proceeding for acquisition and referred to Annexure-G to the petition dated 12.11.1985 showing that the said college has been started in Banchanagar Ahmedia Govt. Primary School scheduled to commence from 7:00 AM to 11:00 AM and submitted that the allegation of running the college on the land in question is contrary to the record and that only in 1991 they sought to trespass into the acquired land for which contempt case No.3 of 1991 was started against Mr. Munsurul Haque and others which is awaiting disposal by this court and with reference to section 96 and sub-section 9 of the State Acquisition & Tenancy Act it is submitted that right, title and interest in the pre-empted case deemed to have been vested in the petitioner although no formal possession has yet been obtained due to the objection of the college authority. Mr. Pal next submitted that being a co-sharer and admitted pre-emptor of the suit property sought to be acquired and the acquisition proceeding being bad in law as aforesaid and partly being used as a graveyard, the petitioner has locus standi to file the application against the illegal acquisition proceeding. 

 6.Mr. Shamsul Alam, the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing for the Respondents, has submitted that though there may be certain irregularities in describing the property in notices under sections 3 and 6 of Ordinance II of 1982, the respondent college has obtained possession of the acquired land with a specific boundary where the Mahila College is presently running. And, as such, irregularity, if there 'be any, has been cured by subsequent delivery of possession. Mr. Alam next submitted that Dr. Momtazuddin Chowdhury has donated the land and the tin-shed for the college and there being a pre-emption proceeding at the instance of the petitioner in respect of the kabala land, the authority was obliged to initiate the proceeding for the public interest to set up Mahila College on the acquired land and as such there is no malafide. Mr. Alam next submitted that the petitioner not being a recorded owner in Khatian, Annexure A and there being no objection from the recorded tenants as to the illegality in the acquisition proceeding, the petitioner has no locus standi to challenge the proceeding in this Court. 

 10. It appears from the aforesaid sections, the relevant rule and the appended forms thereof that the purpose of the issuance of the notices was to intimate the concerned owners or persons to know definitely what part of the land is required out of the big plot of the property sought to be acquired for public purpose, so as to enable them to file objection against the proposed acquisition. In the instant case, as appears from the khatian annexure-A to the petition, that plot No. 3730 in khatian No. 971 comprises 0.71 acres of land and plot No. 3731 in khatian No. 941 comprises 0.47 acres of land and thus the total quantum of land in both the plots is 1.18 acres of land. The copy of the notice under section 3 of the Ordinance in Acquisition Case No.3 of 1985-86 which has been placed before us by the learned Deputy Attorney General go to show the schedule of the acquired land as under: 

 "Part plot No./Nos 3730, and 3731 Area more or less-0.56 acres. Khatian No. 784, 787 and 800. Mouza Banchanagar, JLN 63 Upazila Lakshmipur, District Lakshmipur. Total area more or less 0.56 acres."
